title: We got a foot of snow last night. There's a fresh set of footprints leading from the woods to my back door.
transcript:
We got a foot of snow last night. There's a fresh set of footprints leading from the woods to my back door. I live alone at the end of a dirt road, and the nearest house is a mile away. So when I let the coffee brew and looked out the kitchen window this morning, the footprints stopped me cold.

They came straight out of the tree line, crossed the yard in a perfect line, and ended at my back door. No prints going away.

I told myself it was a hunter who got lost and knocked while I slept. But the back door was still locked, the chain still on.

I went outside to look closer. The boot print had a little star pressed into the heel. I went back in and checked my own boots by the door. Same size. Same star.

And they were wet. Melting snow pooled under them on the mat.

I hadn't left the house in three days.

I sat at the kitchen table trying to think of a reasonable answer, and that was when I noticed the small puddles on the hallway floor. One every few steps, leading away from the back door, past the bathroom, to my bedroom.

The bedroom door is closed. I always leave it open.

The puddles stop right there.
